# Drydock

> Drydock compares built package artifacts and surfaces changed files and
> deterministic supply-chain findings for human review. Package code is never
> executed. Evidence and risk grades are not a guarantee of safety.

## Coding agents

- [Agent quickstart](https://drydock.org/agents): Choose a publisher setup prompt for an existing or new project, or review dependency upgrades.
- [Existing project setup prompt](https://drydock.org/agents/existing-project.md): Walk a maintainer through adding a Drydock review to the current release workflow, starting from the guided setup's draft PR when the GitHub App is installed.
- [New project setup prompt](https://drydock.org/agents/new-project.md): Walk a maintainer through a build-once GitHub Actions release whose publish job waits for approval in Drydock.
- [Project instruction](https://drydock.org/agents/package-review.md): Copyable AGENTS.md instruction, query parameters, response fields, limits, and handling for missing or untrusted evidence.
- [Package diff](https://drydock.org/diff): Human-readable comparisons of public npm, PyPI, and atpm releases, without an account.

## Maintainer setup

- [Docs](https://drydock.org/docs): Review model, GitHub workflow gates, npm staging, and dependency PR links.
- [Security model](https://drydock.org/security): Isolation, credential boundaries, and evidence limitations.
- [Open source](https://drydock.org/open-source): Apache-2.0 source and self-hosting references.

The dependency-review instruction uses the existing public package-diff API. It needs no
account or API key and sends no registry credentials. Use it for public packages
only when the project permits contacting an external service. Authenticated
organization APIs and unlisted report links have separate access boundaries.

Publisher setup is different: it requires maintainer-owned GitHub/registry
configuration and appropriate account access. Setup prompts grant no authority.
Workflow Gates (the GitHub Actions integration) hold only the configured protected job; npm Stage Watchtower
is advisory and cannot block npm approval or every alternate publish path.
